lessons.title: The Alphabet: Capital and Small Letters
lessons.notes_html:
The Alphabet

In this unit we learn the alphabet, letter sounds, tracing lines and writing capital and small letters. English is written from left to right.

Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff, Gg, Hh, Ii, Jj, Kk, Ll, Mm, Nn, Oo, Pp, Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt, Uu, Vv, Ww, Xx, Yy, Zz.

  • Capital letters are big letters.
  • Small letters are little letters.
  • Every letter has its own sound. We say the sound of each letter when we read it.

Key Points

The alphabet is a set of letters. We can write each letter of the alphabet as a small letter or as a capital letter.

mcqs.why: The alphabet list begins with Aa, so A is the very first letter of the alphabet.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a capital letter?
mcqs.why: G is written as a big letter, so it is a capital letter; the others are small letters.

lessons.title: Letters Before and After
lessons.notes_html:
Before and After

  • The letter before B is A and the letter after B is C.
  • The letter before M is L and the letter after M is N.
  • The letter before E is D and the letter after E is F.
  • The letter before Y is X and the letter after Y is Z.

Key Points

Every letter of the alphabet has a letter before it and a letter after it. Learning the order of the letters helps us read and write words.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes just after B?

mcqs.q: Which letter comes just after E?

mcqs.q: Which letter comes just before Y?
mcqs.why: The lesson says the letter before Y is X and the letter after Y is Z.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes just after Y?
mcqs.why: Z is the last letter and it comes right after Y, as the lesson tells us.

mcqs.q: Which letter comes just after D?
mcqs.why: D comes just before E in the alphabet, so the letter after D is E.

mcqs.q: Learning the order of the letters helps us to ______.
mcqs.why: The Key Points say that learning the order of letters helps us read and write words.

lessons.title: Trace and Copy Words

mcqs.why: Hen is spelled h-e-n, exactly three letters, and it appears in the lesson's word list.

lessons.title: Reading: Sa'ad and His Family
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

My name is Sa'ad. I am six years old. I live with my parents, grandparents, two brothers and a sister. I am in class one. I go to school in the morning. I eat my lunch during the break after washing my hands with soap and water. I come back home at one o'clock. First, I do my homework. Then, I play with my brothers and sister in the evening. I love to have dinner with my family. Every night, my mother tells me a bedtime story. Then, I go to sleep.

Remember

  • Sa'ad has one sister.
  • When Sa'ad comes back home from school, he washes his hands with soap and water and does his homework.
  • Sa'ad is six years old.
  • Sa'ad washes his hands with soap and water.
  • Sa'ad's mother tells him a bedtime story.

Key Points

This is an orange. Its leaves are green. I like it.

mcqs.why: The story says, 'My name is Sa'ad. I am six years old,' so Sa'ad is six.

mcqs.q: In which class is Sa'ad?

mcqs.q: How many brothers does Sa'ad have?
mcqs.why: The story says Sa'ad lives with his parents, grandparents, two brothers and a sister.

mcqs.q: How many sisters does Sa'ad have?
mcqs.why: The Remember points confirm that Sa'ad has one sister and two brothers.

mcqs.q: When does Sa'ad go to school?
mcqs.why: The story says, 'I go to school in the morning,' and he comes back at one o'clock.

mcqs.q: What does Sa'ad wash his hands with?
mcqs.why: Sa'ad washes his hands with soap and water before lunch and after coming home.

mcqs.q: At what time does Sa'ad come back home from school?
mcqs.why: The story says, 'I come back home at one o'clock,' after his school day ends.

mcqs.q: What does Sa'ad do first when he comes back home?
mcqs.why: The story says, 'First, I do my homework. Then, I play with my brothers and sister.'

mcqs.q: Who tells Sa'ad a bedtime story every night?
mcqs.why: The story says, 'Every night, my mother tells me a bedtime story. Then, I go to sleep.'

mcqs.q: When does Sa'ad play with his brothers and sister?
mcqs.why: After finishing his homework, Sa'ad plays with his brothers and sister in the evening.

lessons.title: Learning to Spell
lessons.notes_html:

lessons.title: Grammar: Nouns and Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Nouns (Naming Words)

Where is my train? I like my home. Sa'ad is going to school in the morning. The naming words are train, home and school.

Pronouns (Substitution Words)

  • I am Umar. I am a boy.
  • Hi, Anna! You look nice.
  • Mithu is a parrot. It is green.
  • Hira and I are friends. We are in class one.
  • Haris is my brother. He is a good boy.
  • Samita and Asma are sisters. They are girls.
  • Sidra is my friend. She is a girl.

Pronouns in Sentences

  • She is a girl.
  • You are a student.
  • He is a good boy.
  • We are in class one.
  • I am a teacher.
  • It is a rabbit.

mcqs.q: Naming words are called ______.
mcqs.why: The lesson calls naming words nouns; train, home and school are naming words.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a naming word (noun)?
mcqs.why: Train is a thing that we can name, so it is a noun; the others are not naming words.

mcqs.q: In 'Sa'ad is going to school', which word is a naming word?
mcqs.why: The lesson points out train, home and school as the naming words in these sentences.

mcqs.q: Words like I, you, he, she and it are called ______.
mcqs.why: The lesson calls I, you, he, she, it, we and they pronouns — substitution words.

mcqs.q: Mithu is a parrot. ______ is green.
mcqs.why: For a parrot, an animal, we use the pronoun It: 'Mithu is a parrot. It is green.'

mcqs.q: Haris is my brother. ______ is a good boy.
mcqs.why: Haris is a boy, so we use He for him: 'He is a good boy,' as the lesson shows.

mcqs.q: Sidra is my friend. ______ is a girl.
mcqs.why: Sidra is a girl, so the correct pronoun is She: 'She is a girl.'

mcqs.q: Hira and I are friends. ______ are in class one.
mcqs.why: When we speak about ourselves with others, we use We: 'We are in class one.'

mcqs.q: Samita and Asma are sisters. ______ are girls.
mcqs.why: For two or more other people we use They: 'They are girls,' as in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Hi, Anna! ______ look nice.
mcqs.why: When we talk to a person face to face, we use You: 'You look nice.'

lessons.title: Reading: The Poem — Cobbler, Cobbler
lessons.notes_html:
The Poem

Cobbler, cobbler, mend my shoe. Get it done by half past two. Half past two is much too late! Get it done by half past eight. Stitch it up and stitch it down. And I'll give you half a crown.

Remember

  • The boy went to the cobbler to get his shoe mended.
  • The pairs of rhyming words in the poem are: shoe and two, down and crown, eight and late.

Complete the Poem

Cobbler, cobbler, mend my shoe. Stitch it up and stitch it down. Half past two is much too late! Get it done by half past eight. And I'll give you half a crown.

mcqs.q: In the poem, who mends the shoe?
mcqs.why: The poem begins 'Cobbler, cobbler, mend my shoe,' so the cobbler mends the shoe.

mcqs.q: What does the boy want the cobbler to mend?
mcqs.why: The boy says 'mend my shoe,' so he wants his shoe mended by the cobbler.

mcqs.q: The boy first asks to get the shoe done by half past ______.
mcqs.why: The poem says, 'Get it done by half past two,' before the boy changes the time.

mcqs.q: Half past two is much too ______.
mcqs.why: The poem says, 'Half past two is much too late!' so the time must be changed.

mcqs.q: By what time does the boy finally want the shoe done?
mcqs.why: The boy says, 'Get it done by half past eight,' because half past two is too late.

mcqs.q: What will the boy give the cobbler for mending the shoe?
mcqs.why: The last line of the poem says, 'And I'll give you half a crown.'

mcqs.q: Complete the line: 'Stitch it up and stitch it ______.'
mcqs.why: The poem's line is 'Stitch it up and stitch it down,' as given in the poem.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words rhymes in the poem?
mcqs.why: The Remember points list the rhyming pairs: shoe and two, down and crown, eight and late.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words rhymes in the poem?
mcqs.why: Down and crown are one of the rhyming pairs named in the lesson's Remember points.

mcqs.q: Why did the boy go to the cobbler?
mcqs.why: The lesson says the boy went to the cobbler to get his shoe mended.

lessons.title: Word Meanings
lessons.notes_html:

mcqs.q: Who repairs our shoes?

mcqs.why: The poem ends, 'And I'll give you half a crown,' and crown here means a coin.

lessons.title: Grammar: Sentences, Nouns and Action Words
lessons.notes_html:
Sentences in the Correct Order

  • I am a cobbler.
  • You are a teacher.
  • It is my black shoe.
  • We play together.
  • He is a doctor.
  • She is very beautiful.
  • They are standing.

Nouns and Action Words

  • The boy goes to the cobbler. Nouns: boy, cobbler. Action word: goes.
  • Maryam is going to the park. Nouns: Maryam, park. Action word: going.
  • Ali is sleeping in his room. Nouns: Ali, room. Action word: sleeping.
  • I play with my brothers. Noun: brothers. Action word: play.
  • The rabbit jumps. Noun: rabbit. Action word: jumps.

mcqs.q: In 'The boy goes to the cobbler', what is the action word?
mcqs.why: The lesson points out that in this sentence the action word is goes.

mcqs.q: In 'The boy goes to the cobbler', which words are nouns?
mcqs.why: The lesson says the nouns in this sentence are boy and cobbler, and goes is the action word.

mcqs.q: In 'Maryam is going to the park', what is the action word?
mcqs.why: Going shows the action in this sentence; Maryam and park are the nouns.

mcqs.q: In 'Ali is sleeping in his room', which words are nouns?
mcqs.why: The lesson lists Ali and room as the nouns and sleeping as the action word.

mcqs.q: In 'The rabbit jumps', what is the action word?
mcqs.why: Jumps tells us what the rabbit does, so it is the action word in the sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'I play with my brothers', which word is a noun?
mcqs.why: The lesson says brothers is the noun and play is the action word in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an action word?
mcqs.why: Sleeping shows an action; room, boy and park are naming words, that is, nouns.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a naming word (noun)?
mcqs.why: Park names a place, so it is a noun; the others are action words.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct sentence?
mcqs.why: Words must be in the correct order to make a sentence: 'He is a doctor.'

mcqs.q: In 'We play together', what is the action word?
mcqs.why: Play tells us the action in 'We play together'; it matches 'I play with my brothers.'

lessons.title: Creative Writing: People Who Help Us
lessons.notes_html:
People and Their Work

  • A person who mends shoes is a cobbler.
  • A person who teaches is a teacher.
  • A person who treats ill people is a doctor.
  • A person who works in a garden is a gardener.

The Correct Pronouns

  • Hira and Asma are playing. They are good friends.
  • Vicky is a boy. He is a good student.

lessons.title: Reading: Pencil Shaving Artwork
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

Huma is a good girl. She likes helping others. Today, she is helping her sister Hina. They are making flowers with pencil shavings. Things we need: lead pencil, sharpener, colour pencils, glue, a paper, a pair of scissors. Method: 1. Sharpen the colour pencils. 2. Collect the pencil shavings. 3. Take a piece of paper and draw small flowers on it with a lead pencil. 4. Use glue to paste the pencil shavings on the flowers.

Remember

  • Huma helped her sister Hina in making pencil shaving artwork.
  • Before collecting the pencil shavings, they sharpened the colour pencils.
  • Two things we need are a lead pencil and a sharpener. We also need colour pencils, glue, a paper and a pair of scissors.
  • We use scissors for cutting paper.
  • They need six things to complete their artwork.
  • Hina draws some flowers on paper.

lessons.title: Reading: Fruits and Vegetables
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

One day, fruits and vegetables met together in a basket. They became friends. All of them were talking to one another, but Red Carrot was sitting quietly in a corner. Yellow Mango asked, Why are you sad? Red Carrot said, Juicy Apple always fights with me. He says he is very sweet and healthy. People like to eat him more than me. Yellow Mango said, You should not feel sad. Allah has blessed us with good health. We should not fight. Juicy Apple said sorry to Red Carrot for being rude to her and they became friends again.

Remember

  • Red Carrot was sad.
  • Juicy Apple said that he is very sweet and healthy and people like to eat him more than Red Carrot.
  • No, it is not good to make fun of others. We should be kind to everyone.
  • All fruits and vegetables are good for health.
  • Carrot was sitting quietly in a corner.
  • Apple said sorry to Carrot for being rude to her.

Sentences in the Correct Order

  • Apple always fights with me.
  • He makes fun of me.
  • They became friends.
  • Fruits were talking to one another.

mcqs.q: What did Juicy Apple say to Red Carrot at the end?
mcqs.why: Juicy Apple said sorry to Red Carrot for being rude to her, and they became friends.

mcqs.why: The story says Carrot was sitting quietly in a corner of the basket.

mcqs.why: After Apple said sorry, they became friends again, as the story ends.

lessons.title: Grammar: Proper Nouns and Question Words
lessons.notes_html:

Maham is drinking. We live in Lahore. Jawad is running. The proper nouns are Maham, Lahore and Jawad. More proper nouns: Anna lives in Islamabad. His father's name is Zafar. They are going to visit Naran. Waqas is my best friend. Sidra was sleeping.

Question Words

  • What is your favourite vegetable?
  • Where are you going?
  • Who is playing in the garden?

Key Points

We use what to ask about a thing, where to ask about a place and who to ask about a person.

lessons.title: Reading: Zara's First Day at School
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

It was Monday morning. Zara went to her new school where she met her class teacher. Assalaam-o-Alaikum! I am Zara. Today is my first day in this school. Wa Alaikum-us-Salam! I am Anum, your grade 1 English teacher. Welcome to the school. Miss Anum and Zara went to the class. All students welcomed her and introduced themselves one at a time. Then, they explained the classroom rules.

Classroom Manners

  • Keep your classroom clean.
  • Respect your teachers.
  • Listen to your teachers carefully.
  • Share your things with your classmates.
  • Seek permission before going to the washroom or to drink water.
  • Be polite and use please and thank you.
  • Raise your hand and wait for your turn.
  • Complete your work on time.
  • Make a queue during break and off time.

Remember

  • Zara was new in the school.
  • Miss Anum teaches English to grade 1.
  • Miss Anum is the English teacher of grade 1.
  • Keep your classroom clean.
  • Listen to your teacher carefully.
  • Respect your teacher.

lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

One day, all the animals of the jungle were having fun together. A hare told them proudly that he could run very fast. He was making fun of a tortoise for his slow speed. The tortoise challenged the hare to have a race. The hare happily agreed. The race started. The hare ran very fast and left the tortoise far behind. I have much time to reach the finish line. I can have some rest, he thought. So he slept under a tree. The tortoise kept walking slowly. At last, he reached the finish line. The animals loudly cheered for the tortoise. The hare woke up from his sleep. The poor hare ran to reach the finish line, but it was too late. The tortoise was over the line. The hare was very sad at the end because he lost the match.

Remember

lessons.title: Grammar: Possession, Question Mark and Commands
lessons.notes_html:
Words Showing Possession

Question Mark

Key Points

We use a question mark at the end of a question.

lessons.title: Reading: The Poem — My Kitty Cat
lessons.notes_html:
The Poem

My Kitty Cat, by Ryan Gibbs. My kitty cat is black and white. She sleeps all day and plays all night. At dawn she knows when to be fed And walks atop my sleepy head. Once she finally gets her food, She soon adopts a happy mood. Then in the chair she likes the best, She stretches out to take a rest.

Remember

  • The colour of the kitty cat is black and white.
  • The cat sleeps all day and plays all night.
  • The cat had a rest in the chair she likes the best.
  • The kitty cat eats its food at dawn.
  • The kitty cat wants to have a rest on the chair.

lessons.title: Grammar: Comma; Calendar; Capital Letters
lessons.notes_html:
Comma

  • I love to eat apples, grapes, mangoes and bananas.
  • My best friends are Sana, Iqra, Asma and Esha.
  • I have two storybooks, five pencils, one pen and a scrapbook.
  • She bought biscuits, chips, pizza and juice from the market.
  • He is a strong, wealthy and healthy man.
  • The plain cake requires flour, sugar, eggs, butter and vanilla essence.

Key Points

We use a comma to separate three or more words in a series.

Calendar

There are twelve months in a year. The sixth month of a year is June. The months are January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.

Capital Letters and Punctuation

  • Why are you going to Islamabad?
  • This is my cat, Kitty.
  • What is your favourite toy?
  • He is a police officer.

I love to eat apples grapes, mangoes and bananas.
mcqs.why: Commas separate the items in the list: apples, grapes, mangoes and bananas.

lessons.title: Grammar: His, Her, Their; Comma; Commands
